firstNullToZeroLayer.FIRST_NULL_TO_ZERO_LAYER: api/services/partsDataCache.cjs, in the read() loop: `const price = record.price || 0;`
firstNullToZeroLayer.NULL_TO_ZERO_ROOT_CAUSE: That expression is the first place where a formal catalogue NULL price silently becomes numeric 0, and it produces `partsByModel`, which is exactly the input costEngine resolves prices from. Because 0 is correctly a VALID formal price (schema `REAL DEFAULT 0` plus `CHECK(price IS NULL OR price >= 0)`, partCommands parseNonNegativeNumber, partQueries price filter lower bound 0), the coercion destroyed the distinction between 'unpriced' and 'zero cost'. An unpriced part therefore contributed 0 with missingParts empty, cost.complete became true, and same-read-set scenario comparison fabricated a COMPARABLE result with a non-null delta.
firstNullToZeroLayer.howItWasFound: A direct trace of the failing fixture into calculateRecipeCost showed the packing row arriving with NO snapshotPrice field at all, which meant the price could only come from partsByModel, and partsByModel is built by partsDataCache.
NULL_TO_ZERO_FIX: api/services/partsDataCache.cjs - partsByModel now preserves null/undefined exactly; zero passes through untouched; non-numeric values are left for the formal rule to judge. partsCache (the per-model single-value index read by box_type inference and similar existing callers, all of which read it through `Number(x || 0)`) keeps its previous 0 semantics, so that behaviour is deliberately unchanged.

api/services/costEngine.cjs - hasUsableCatalogPrice() and catalogPriceSourceLabel() are now EXPORTED so the price rule has exactly one definition (verified: exactly one `function hasUsableCatalogPrice` exists in api/).
api/services/dynamicCostPreview.cjs - buildPackingSnapshotParts no longer fabricates `snapshotPrice: 0` from an unusable catalogue price, and consumes the shared rule instead of an inline duplicate.

api/services/recipeBomEngine.cjs - the optional-part row and the packing row no longer fabricate a snapshotPrice from an unusable catalogue price; the local duplicate of the price rule is deleted. This includes the catalogue-identity site that the failing fixture actually uses.
firstNullToZeroLayer.representationNote: No hasPrice / priceState / isPriced marker was added. The existing `null` value in the existing `partsByModel[].price` field carries the missing state, and the existing `missingParts` channel carries it outward. A new field was therefore unnecessary and a DB schema/migration change was avoided.

priceStateContract.PRICE_STATE_REPRESENTATION: the raw numeric value, with `null`/`undefined` preserved as the missing state and non-finite or negative values judged invalid by the single shared rule
priceStateContract.PRICE_POSITIVE_POLICY: VALID_PRICE - contribution price x qty, missingParts empty, source 精确匹配 or 型号回退(取最低价)
priceStateContract.PRICE_ZERO_POLICY: VALID_PRICE - contribution 0, missingParts empty. Zero is a legal zero-cost catalogue price and is NEVER treated as missing merely because it is zero. Identical outcome to production master.
priceStateContract.PRICE_NEGATIVE_POLICY: INVALID_DATA - contribution 0, reported in missingParts, source 正式目录价格无效. Production master instead produced a negative total.
priceStateContract.PRICE_NULL_POLICY: MISSING_PRICE - contribution 0, reported in missingParts, source 正式目录未定价, costComplete false
priceStateContract.PRICE_NON_NUMERIC_POLICY: INVALID_DATA - a NaN or non-numeric price contributes 0 and is reported in missingParts. Production master produced NaN in the detail price and NaN in the total.
priceStateContract.noTruthinessChecks: verified - the rule is `value !== null && value !== undefined && value !== '' && Number.isFinite(Number(value)) && Number(value) >= 0`, so a valid zero is never dropped by a falsy check
priceStateContract.SUPPLIER_FALLBACK_ALL_MISSING_CASE: PASS - [null, undefined], [-1, null] and ['abc', null] all yield no available formal price, contribute 0 and report the part in missingParts
priceStateContract.MISSING_PARTS_SEMANTICS: unchanged formal channel - currentRecipeCost derives costComplete from missingParts.length === 0 and keeps the existing warning text
priceStateContract.PARTIAL_COST_SEMANTICS: unchanged - partialTotalCost is still returned, currentTotalCost stays null while incomplete
priceStateContract.singleCostImplementation: costEngine remains the only formal cost implementation; no second algorithm and no fork in scenarioComparison
